source: The single source for every "what if I did X" in the app: one line a lever, the size of each move stated as a plain assumption. A side hustle netting $500 a month, a house hack cutting the rent line by 40%, a move somewhere a quarter cheaper, a job change worth 20% more, a 3% real raise kept or spent. Illustrative starting points chosen to be arguable, not measured averages; every room that offers a lever prints its figure beside the number it moves and lets it be changed.
confidenceNote: Teaching devices. No study says a house hack cuts housing by 40% for you; it says it can. The figures are the defaults a room starts from, never findings.
note: Read by shared/levers.js. No room may inline a lever figure again (D-174). `moves` values: absolute cents when the key ends in `Cents`, otherwise a share of the current figure, positive or negative. `appliesWhen` is one of a few fixed phrases the library knows how to read; it is not evaluated as code. Implied hourly wage = monthly gain ÷ (hoursPerWeek × 4.33), computed in the library.
